draft.title: Predicting spontaneity
card: In ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, T is always positive. So the signs of ΔH and ΔS decide how ΔG changes with temperature.
ΔG is always negative. The reaction is spontaneous at all temperatures.
ΔG is always positive. The reaction is spontaneous at no temperature.
Temperature decides. If both are negative, the reaction is spontaneous at low temperatures. If both are positive, it is spontaneous at high temperatures.
draft.remember: Opposite signs fix the answer. Matching signs mean temperature decides.

a.q: A reaction has a positive ΔH and a positive ΔS. When is it spontaneous?
a.why: At high temperature the TΔS term is large and positive, so it outweighs ΔH and makes ΔG negative. At low temperature ΔH dominates, so ΔG is positive.
a.clue: Which term gets larger as T rises?

b.q: Water vapour condenses to liquid water, releasing heat. At which temperatures is condensation spontaneous?
b.why: Condensing releases heat, so ΔH is negative. The particles become more ordered, so ΔS is negative. With both negative, the -TΔS term is positive and grows with T, so ΔG is negative only at low temperatures.
b.clue: Decide the sign of ΔS for gas becoming liquid.

check.summary: No problems found. Both intended answers are correct: (a) is spontaneous only at high temperatures, and (b), condensation with negative ΔH and ΔS, only at low temperatures.
